bauta-mask.context: A full face mask with a square jutting chin and no mouth, worn under a three cornered hat. Used for Venetian carnival themes, masquerades, historical costume and anonymity.

bed-head-face.context: A sleepy yawning face with one eye half open and messy hair tufts sticking up. Used for waking up, mornings, tiredness, bad hair days and just out of bed moments.

brain-freeze-face.context: A face grimacing with eyes squeezed shut next to an ice cream cone. Used for brain freeze, cold treats, sudden headaches and summer dessert humour.

disgusted-face.context: A disgusted face with lowered brows, squinting eyes and the tongue pushed out of a downturned mouth. Used for gross, yuck and distaste reactions, bad food and unpleasant content.

distorted-face.context: A warped face with a wavy outline, mismatched eyes and a skewed mouth. Used for dizzy, woozy or glitched states, distortion filters and feeling out of sorts.

emotion-recognition.context: A face inside four scanning corners with a small smile and a small frown beside it. Used for emotion detection, sentiment analysis, mood tracking and affective computing features.

eyes-in-the-dark.context: Two glowing almond eyes with slit pupils staring out of a dark rounded shape. Used for night, hidden creatures, horror and Halloween themes, stealth and being watched.

face-swap.context: Two small faces with curved arrows swapping them between each other. Used for face swap filters, photo and video editing apps, avatar switching and deepfake topics.

face-without-mouth.context: A round face with two eyes and no mouth at all. Used for speechless and no comment reactions, silence, being lost for words and quiet or mute states.

facial-landmarks.context: A face mesh made of landmark points on the jaw, eyes, nose and mouth joined by lines. Used for face tracking, computer vision, AR filters, biometrics and machine learning tools.

hangover-face.context: A face with droopy half closed eyes, a wavy queasy mouth and an ice pack resting on top of the head. Used for hangovers, headaches, the morning after and feeling unwell.

kilroy-was-here.context: A bald head with a long nose peeking over a wall, with fingers gripping the edge. The classic graffiti doodle, used for peeking, easter eggs, retro humour and 'I was here' messages.

krampus-mask.context: A carved horned mask with long twisted horns, shaggy fur and a long hanging tongue. Used for winter folklore, alpine festivals, Christmas season horror themes and costume events.

mad-scientist-face.context: A face with wild frizzy hair, goggles pushed up on the forehead and a manic grin. Used for science experiments, crazy ideas, invention, labs and evil genius themes.

moai-head.context: A tall stone head seen from the front with a heavy brow, a long nose, long ears and a jutting chin. Used for monuments, travel to Rapa Nui, ancient sculpture and mystery themes.

ogre-face.context: A broad ogre face with small ears, a heavy brow, a wide flat nose and two tusks rising from the lower lip. Used for fantasy games, fairy tales, monster characters and role playing.

olmec-head.context: A colossal round stone head wearing a fitted helmet cap, with full lips and a broad flat nose. Used for Mesoamerican history, archaeology, museums and ancient civilisations.

pierrot-face.context: A round white clown face with a black skullcap, a painted tear under one eye and a ruffled collar. Used for mime, pantomime, circus, theatre and melancholy themes.

proud-face.context: A proud face with the chin raised, closed eyes, a satisfied smile and a small sparkle. Used for pride, achievement, smug satisfaction and celebrating a job well done.

pulling-eyelid-face.context: A face pulling down one lower eyelid with a fingertip while sticking out its tongue. Used for teasing and mocking reactions, playful taunts and cheeky chat stickers.

punk-face.context: A head in profile with a tall spiked mohawk and a sneer. Used for punk music and fashion, rebellion, subculture, attitude and edgy themes.

side-eye-face.context: A face glancing sideways with both pupils shifted to one side, one raised brow and a flat mouth. Used for suspicious, skeptical or judging reactions in chat and comments.

stress-ball.context: A squishy ball with a strained face squeezed in a fist. Used for stress relief, anxiety and wellbeing topics, fidget toys and workplace tension.

thumbing-nose-face.context: A face thumbing its nose with the fingers spread wide and the tongue sticking out. Used for taunting, mocking and cheeky reactions, pranks and playful defiance.

twitching-eye-face.context: A face with a tense forced smile and one eye twitching, marked by zigzag lines. Used for stress, being on edge, barely holding it together and passive aggressive calm.

vejigante-mask.context: A festival mask with cone shaped horns sprouting all around the head, fierce eyes and a toothy mouth. Used for carnival and folk festival themes, Caribbean culture and costume art.

volto-mask.context: A plain full face carnival mask with almond eye holes, a straight nose, closed lips and ribbon ties. Used for masquerade parties, carnival events, theatre and costume shops.

weary-face.context: A weary face with eyes squeezed shut, brows tilted up and a wide open wailing mouth. Used for exhausted, fed up and distraught reactions, burnout and frustration.
